narr: A weak area of high pressure was centered over eastern New Mexico on August 31, 2021, which allowed for a weak monsoon moisture plume to begin to develop across the area. Moisture values were highest across southern New Mexico, and as daytime heating destabilized the atmosphere, a typical monsoon day was observed across much of northern and central New Mexico. With the deepest moisture across southern New Mexico, the thunderstorms that developed in this area were the most capable of producing heavy rainfall. One thunderstorm near Capitan produced heavy rainfall in a short period of time that caused the Oso Creek to briefly overfill its banks, causing flooding in the area.
ev: Heavy rain caused Oso Creek to overfill its banks and overtop Dawson Road. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that Dawson Road was flooded for about 20 to 30 minutes. No damages are known.
lsr: OSO CREEK OVERTOPPED DAWSON ROAD FOR 20-30 MINUTES.
